prompt.context: The maker of Botox is considering expanding to the migraine market and has already begun clinical trials in this area. The product is expected to receive FDA approval in 2019. Your team has been hired to assess the viability of this product for launch.
prompt.question: How will you determine if the market is attractive? If the market is attractive, do you have any recommendations regarding how to launch the product? What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch?

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the drug?
clarifying_info.a: The drug will be priced at $200 per injection.
Remaining development and launch costs are approximately $5B. Manufacturing marginal costs are expected to be quite small. Annual marketing expense can be estimated at $1B.

clarifying_info.q: How is the drug administered and how often?
clarifying_info.a: It is a prophylactic injection given every 2 months.

clarifying_info.q: How does the product compare to existing treatments?
clarifying_info.a: It offers similar efficacy compared to the market leading option but without any side effects. When taken for migraines it also has some added skin care benefits.
The market leading branded prescription oral migraine treatment lost patent protection last year. There is a strong over-the-counter generic market for migraine treatments.

clarifying_info.q: What geography should we focus on?
clarifying_info.a: The drug will initially be produced in the US, so use the US population of 320 million.

framework: 1. Market sizing: Estimate the size of the US prescription migraine market and Botox's revenue potential
2. Profitability assessment: Evaluate revenue vs. costs (development, launch, annual marketing) to determine viability
3. Launch considerations: Assess branding, cannibalization, competition, regulatory, and patient adoption risks
4. Recommendation: Decide whether to launch and under what brand/pricing strategy

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the US prescription migraine market and Botox's potential annual revenue.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use a top-down approach: US population → % chronic migraine sufferers → % with severe migraines needing prescription treatment → total patients × annual revenue per patient × Botox market share. Key assumptions to probe: 1 in 7 people suffer migraines (~15%), 25% of those have severe migraines requiring prescription treatment, Botox captures ~30% market share within 5 years.

math.setup: US population × % chronic sufferers × % severe × price per injection × injections per year × Botox market share
steps: Price per injection: $200; injections per year: 12 months / 2 months = 6
math.answer: Botox's potential annual revenue is approximately $4.32B

questions.prompt: Is this market financially attractive given the cost structure?
questions.guidance: Annual revenue of ~$4.32B vs. $1B annual marketing expense gives ~$3.32B annual operating contribution before amortizing the $5B development/launch cost. $5B one-time cost recoverable in roughly 1.5 years at that contribution level — financially very attractive. Candidate should note manufacturing marginal costs are small so contribution margin is high.

math.setup: Annual contribution = Botox revenue − annual marketing; payback period = one-time cost / annual contribution
math.answer: Payback period ~1.5 years; financially very attractive

questions.prompt: What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: (1) Branding — Botox has a cosmetic image; using the same brand for a medical indication may reduce patient willingness and creates shared liability if a new side effect is found in either market; (2) Cannibalization/erosion — if physicians and patients learn the products are essentially the same molecule, it will be hard to maintain two separate markets; launching at a lower price point risks off-label use and price erosion in the cosmetic segment; (3) Competition — similar efficacy to generics may prevent formulary placement by insurers, limiting patient access; (4) Regulatory — new indication of an existing product may require separate labeling, restricted specialties, and separate marketing; (5) Patient behavior — patients are generally averse to injectable therapies when oral alternatives exist; (6) Upside considerations — approval in other countries could increase market size; targeted marketing to a specific patient population with better efficacy could improve positioning.

brainstorming.prompt: What concerns should the client take into consideration before deciding to launch?

categories.name: Branding
ideas: The Botox brand carries a cosmetic/controversial image that may deter patients from using it for a non-cosmetic medical indication
Using the same brand for both products increases shared risk exposure: a side effect discovered in one indication (especially the much larger migraine market) could damage the other

categories.name: Cannibalization and Price Erosion
ideas: If physicians and patients identify the two products as essentially the same, it will be very difficult to maintain separate markets
Launching the migraine product at a lower price point than the cosmetic indication could drive off-label use and significant price erosion in the cosmetic segment

categories.name: Competition and Insurance Coverage
ideas: Similar efficacy vs. generics means insurance companies may decline to include Botox on formulary
Many migraine sufferers may be unable to afford the treatment out-of-pocket if not covered by insurance

categories.name: Regulatory
ideas: Launching a new indication of an existing product for a different condition is regulatory complex
FDA may require different labeling and restrict use to certain specialties, necessitating separate marketing efforts

categories.name: Patient Adoption
ideas: Patients are generally averse to injectable therapies when comparable oral treatments are available
Need to demonstrate clear patient benefit to drive adoption over existing oral generics

categories.name: Strategic Upside
ideas: Filing for approval in other countries could substantially increase addressable market
If efficacy data shows advantage for a specific sub-population, targeted marketing could improve competitive positioning

recommendation: The projected annual revenue of ~$4.32B with a ~1.5-year payback on $5B in launch costs makes this a financially attractive market to enter
However, launching under the Botox brand as currently proposed poses significant cannibalization and reputational risks to the highly profitable cosmetic segment
Launching under a separate brand name would allow more effective differentiation in advertising to customers and physicians, and make differential pricing more defensible
risks: Regulatory: The product has not yet received FDA approval; launch is contingent on regulatory clearance
Branding: Same-brand strategy risks reputational spillover; different-brand strategy risks lack of market traction for a new name
Cannibalization: A lower migraine price point risks substantial off-label use and erosion of the cosmetic segment
next_steps: Continue clinical trials and pursue FDA approval; simultaneously establish regulatory, brand, and marketing-based barriers between the cosmetic and migraine markets
Negotiate contracts with insurance companies to secure formulary placement for the Botox migraine product prior to launch
Evaluate a new brand name strategy to protect cosmetic segment pricing and reputation while building independent market presence for the migraine indication
